q: How many books are in the Bible?
more: 39 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New. This is the Protestant Bible, which includes the King James Version. Catholic Bibles have 46 Old Testament books.

q: How many chapters does the Bible have?
more: 929 in the Old Testament and 260 in the New.

q: How many verses are in the King James Bible?
more: About three in every four are in the Old Testament: 23,145, against 7,957 in the New.

q: What is the shortest verse in the Bible?
more: John 11:35. Two words and nine letters in the King James Version.

q: Which is the longest verse in the Bible?
more: It runs to 90 words in the King James Version.

q: Which chapter is the longest?
more: It has 176 verses. The next longest, Numbers 7, has 89.

q: Which chapter is the shortest?
more: Just two verses.

q: Which chapter sits in the very middle of the Bible?
more: There are 594 chapters before it and 594 after it. It is also the shortest chapter.

q: Does the Bible have a middle verse?
more: The King James Version has an even number of verses, so the middle falls between Psalm 103:1 and Psalm 103:2.

q: Which book has the most chapters?
more: 150 psalms and 2,461 verses, more than any other book.

q: How many books have only one chapter?
more: Obadiah, Philemon, 2 John, 3 John and Jude.

q: Which book has the fewest verses?
more: Only 13 verses. 3 John is next with 14.

q: How many New Testament books are letters?
more: Romans through Jude. The other six are the four Gospels, Acts and Revelation.

q: Why does Psalm 119 have exactly 176 verses?
more: It is a poem in 22 sections of eight verses, one section for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

q: How many chapters are in Proverbs?
more: Enough to read one a day through a long month.

q: What are the first and last words of the Bible?
more: Genesis 1:1 opens with the first; Revelation 22:21 closes with the second.

q: How many times does the word “Bible” appear in the Bible?
more: The word is not used anywhere in the King James text.

q: How often does the word “Christian” appear?
more: Acts 11:26, Acts 26:28 and 1 Peter 4:16, in the King James Version.

q: Where were believers first called Christians?
more: The book of Acts records it in chapter 11.

q: The word “grandmother” appears once. Who is she?
more: Timothy's grandmother, named in 2 Timothy 1:5.

q: How many times does the word “eternity” appear?
more: In Isaiah 57:15, in the King James Version.

q: Which letter of the alphabet is missing from Ezra 7:21?
more: In the King James Version this verse uses every other letter. No verse uses all 26.

q: Which psalm repeats the same verse four times?
more: The same line of praise returns in verses 8, 15, 21 and 31.

q: Which book never uses the word “God”?
more: Neither “God” nor “Lord” appears in it in the King James Version. The Song of Solomon is the only other book where that is so.

q: Who lived the longest in the Bible?
more: 969 years, according to Genesis 5:27.

q: Which animal speaks in the book of Numbers?
more: Balaam's donkey, in Numbers 22:28. The King James Version calls it an ass.

q: How long was the shortest reign of a king in the Bible?
more: Zimri, king of Israel, in 1 Kings 16:15.

q: Which king of Israel or Judah reigned the longest?
more: 55 years in Jerusalem, having begun at the age of twelve.

q: What do the flood, Moses on the mountain and Jesus in the wilderness share?
more: The same span is given for all three.

q: What was the first miracle of Jesus?
more: At a wedding in Cana of Galilee, told in John chapter 2.

q: Where is the Lord's Prayer found?
more: Matthew chapter 6 and Luke chapter 11.

q: Where are the Ten Commandments written?
more: They are given twice.

q: How many New Testament letters open with Paul's name?
more: Romans through Philemon each begin with the word “Paul”.

q: Which books of the Bible are named after women?
more: Two of the 66.

q: Where are the twelve apostles listed by name?
more: The list begins at verse 2.

q: What language was the Old Testament written in?
more: Almost entirely, with a few short passages in Aramaic.

q: What does the word “Bible” mean?
more: It comes from the Greek ta biblia, “the books”.

q: Did King James write the King James Bible?
more: He commissioned it. Records show 47 scholars took part, and it was published in 1611.

q: What was the first book printed with movable metal type in Western Europe?
more: Finished about 1455 in Mainz, Germany. Around 180 copies were printed.

sources.name: Library of Congress: The Gutenberg Bible

q: Who divided the Bible into chapters?
more: The chapters used today are credited to him, an archbishop of Canterbury, in the early 1200s.

q: Which English Bible was the first to number its verses?
more: Published in 1560. The numbering followed the printer Robert Estienne's Greek New Testament of 1551.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Chapters and verses of the Bible

q: Who found the first Dead Sea Scrolls?
more: In 1947, in a cave at Qumran by the Dead Sea. The scrolls include every book of the Hebrew Bible except Esther.

q: Who translated the Bible into Latin?
more: Pope Damasus commissioned him in 382 and he finished about 405. His version is known as the Vulgate.

q: When was the whole Bible first put into English?
more: By John Wycliffe and his followers, in copies written out by hand.

q: When was the New Testament first printed in English?
more: William Tyndale's translation, printed at Worms in Germany.

sources.name: Cambridge University Library: The Bible in English

q: What is the best-selling book of all time?
more: Guinness World Records puts it at an estimated five billion copies or more.

q: Into how many languages has the whole Bible been translated?
more: Wycliffe Global Alliance counted 756 languages with a complete Bible in 2024.

sources.name: Wycliffe Global Alliance: Global Scripture Access
